scheme: one brief per fact-able competency below its floor; target = need x oversample (3x if fact_able<=4 else 1.6x); existing_facts_en = feed cards carrying the code (v2 tags)

briefs.competency: discuss the patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years with family and community members to assess and describe how predictable patterns of eruptions are
recognize the features of a fair test and that scientific investigations also involve doing at least three trials, or use replication, and observing, measuring, and recording accurately
existing_facts_en:
How do you get an accurate reading from a thermometer?

Look at the thermometer at the exact same level as your eye!

briefs.competency: describe the steps of a simple science investigation (What is the problem? What materials do you need? What do you need to do? What have you found out/learned?)
existing_facts_en:
Which nail rusts in the jar experiment?

Only the nail touching both water and air rusts, proving you need both together to make rust!

How do scientists solve mysteries?

They ask a question, make a hypothesis, test it with an experiment, and form a conclusion from the results!

briefs.competency: describe and explain how sound changes when the source or the receiver are moving
existing_facts_en:
Why does an ambulance siren sound high-pitched when it comes near, but lower when it drives away?

Because of the Doppler effect! Sound waves compress as the ambulance approaches, making a higher pitch, and stretch as it recedes, dropping the pitch.

Why does an ambulance siren change pitch as it passes?

It sounds higher coming toward you and lower moving away! The sound waves bunch up when approaching and spread out when leaving—this is the Doppler effect.
content_standard: Properties of water and sound waves

briefs.competency: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the female reproductive system as ovaries, uterus, and vagina and those of the male reproductive system as the prostate, testis, and penis and describe how they work
existing_facts_en: In fertilization, a sex cell from the female (the egg) joins with a sex cell from the male (the sperm) to form a single new cell.
A mother who has been vaccinated or had measles can pass temporary protection to her newborn during its first months — one more reason vaccination matters even before having children.

Can a baby hear sounds before birth?

Yes! In the later months of pregnancy, a baby can already hear sounds, like its mother's voice.
A pregnant mother needs healthy, nutritious food so her baby can grow strong inside her womb.

briefs.competency: identify some examples of longitudinal waves, and transverse waves
existing_facts_en: Earthquakes have a fast P-wave and a slower S-wave! The P-wave reaches sensors first, giving the Philippines an early warning before the damaging S-wave arrives.
Sound is a longitudinal wave! Air particles alternately compress together and spread apart in the exact same direction the sound travels.

Did you know earthquakes make two types of waves?

P waves are faster longitudinal compression waves, while S waves are slower transverse waves that cause more shaking!
In a transverse wave, particles vibrate perpendicular to the wave's travel direction! It's just like waves on a shaken rope or light waves.
During the tinikling dance, the clapping bamboo poles produce sound waves through rapid vibrations in the air!

How do particles move in a longitudinal wave like sound?

They vibrate back and forth in the exact same direction the wave travels!

How do particles move in a transverse wave like a water wave?

They vibrate up and down, at right angles to the direction the wave travels!
content_standard: Properties of water and sound waves

briefs.competency: gather information from local indigenous community members or from reliable secondary sources to investigate ways that indigenous people of the Philippines represented and communicated understandings of the predictability of solar and lunar eclipses, and patterns/interpretations in the night sky and their use for tracking time
existing_facts_en: Orion is a famous constellation shaped like a hunter, with three stars in a row called Orion's Belt. In the Philippines, some native stories call it Balatik — a hunting trap!

How did Filipino farmers know when to plant crops?

Long ago, they used constellations like Balatik as a sky calendar! Their appearance signaled the coming of the rains.
A constellation is a cool pattern or shape formed by a group of stars in the night sky!

How did old-time Filipinos predict the weather?

They watched natural signs! 'A ring around the moon means rain' and 'many ants moving means rain is coming' — modern science confirms some of these!

How do some calendars track months using the Moon?

Many traditional calendars like the Islamic and Chinese calendars base their months on the lunar month — the Moon's phase cycle. A lunar month is about 29.5 days, shorter than a solar month!

How do the Tagbanua people of Palawan use the stars?

They use the Balatik constellation, the local name for Orion’s Belt, to navigate and track the seasons!
Ancient Filipino sailors used constellations like the North Star to navigate their wooden balangay boats across the vast ocean!
The Tagbanua people of Palawan recognize the Balatik constellation, which is the same as the Orion constellation in Western astronomy!
Filipinos call the Orion constellation "Balatik"! It is a prominent three-star pattern that is super visible during the dry season.

briefs.competency: carry out investigations with water waves in a ripple tank and observe and describe the features of the waves including shape (crests and troughs), size (width and height), and patterns of movement (how they bend, or reflect off walls)
existing_facts_en: Most snakes move in an S-shaped curve, like a wave flowing from head to tail.
An echo happens when sound waves bounce off a big wall or mountain and come right back to us!

How does radar track objects?

Radar sends out a radio wave and waits for it to bounce back from an airplane or cloud! By checking how fast it returns, it knows the object's distance and speed.

How fast can a tsunami travel in the deep ocean?

A tsunami zooms as fast as a jet plane in deep water! The deeper the ocean, the faster it goes. Near shore, it slows down but grows super tall!

Why do recording studios put soft things on their walls and ceilings?

Soft materials like foam, curtains, and carpet absorb sound and reduce echo! This keeps the studio quiet and clear.

Do ocean waves actually push water forward?

No! Waves carry mechanical energy across vast distances, but water particles only move in circles, not forward!

How do recording studios reduce echoes?

Acoustic foam panels absorb sound waves to reduce echoes inside a recording studio!
A wave carries energy through the water, but the water doesn't travel! It just moves up and down as the energy passes by.
Earthquake shaking spreads outward from where it started, just like water ripples when you drop a stone!
Normal ocean waves might be one meter high, but a massive tsunami wave can reach heights of over 30 meters!
content_standard: Properties of water and sound waves

briefs.competency: identify differences and similarities between longitudinal waves and transverse waves
existing_facts_en: Sound is a pressure wave needing a medium like air, water, or solid, so it cannot travel through a complete vacuum!
Sound is a longitudinal wave! Air particles alternately compress together and spread apart in the exact same direction the sound travels.

What happens to air particles in a compression and rarefaction?

In a compression, air particles are bunched close together with high pressure. In a rarefaction, particles are spread apart with low pressure!

Did you know earthquakes make two types of waves?

P waves are faster longitudinal compression waves, while S waves are slower transverse waves that cause more shaking!

How do polarized sunglasses reduce glare?

Normal light vibrates in all directions. Polarized sunglasses only let light vibrating in one direction pass through, blocking glare from smooth surfaces!
In a transverse wave, particles vibrate perpendicular to the wave's travel direction! It's just like waves on a shaken rope or light waves.

How do particles move in a longitudinal wave like sound?

They vibrate back and forth in the exact same direction the wave travels!

How do particles move in a transverse wave like a water wave?

They vibrate up and down, at right angles to the direction the wave travels!
During the compression stage of a sound wave, a vibrating object pushes air molecules closely together!

What makes up an electromagnetic wave?

It's a transverse wave made of a changing electric field and magnetic field traveling together, vibrating at right angles to its motion!
content_standard: Properties of water and sound waves

briefs.competency: participate in guided activities to explore and describe some ways to use movement, sound, and light to send information between two people
existing_facts_en:
How do sperm whales talk to each other?

Besides finding food, sperm whales use patterns of clicks to 'talk' with their family!
In the Philippines, especially in Palawan's mangrove trees, certain fireflies flash in perfect unison — a spectacular natural light show!
Parrots are noisy birds — they use loud calls to talk with the rest of their flock.

How does a smoke detector keep us safe?

A smoke detector sounds an alarm when it senses smoke, giving an early warning before a fire grows!
In a tin-can telephone, sound travels along the tight string as vibrations — like a secret message highway!
A periscope is a clever tube with two angled mirrors inside. It bounces light from above down to your eye — so you can peek over walls or see outside a submarine!
The kubing is a beautiful indigenous instrument from Mindanao! Used for storytelling, courtship, and relaxation, it is a perfect example of the physics of sound in Filipino culture.
In some indigenous communities, the kubing is used for courtship! Since its soft sound is only heard up close, it acts like a secret conversation. A real-life physics of sound example!
On a traffic light, red signals stop, yellow means get ready, and green means it is safe to go!
On a traffic light, red means stop, yellow means slow down or get ready, and green means go!
Fiber optic cables transmit pulses of light to carry our internet and telephone data over very long distances!

briefs.competency: recognize that the non-living materials that make up the environment are referred to as 'earth materials'
existing_facts_en: Some carbon stays locked away for a very long time inside rocks like limestone.
A single large parrotfish can produce over 90 kilograms of white sand a year by chewing coral skeleton — many famous white sand beaches are largely made of sand from parrotfish!

Where do glass and ceramic come from?

Both come from earth materials! Sand is used for glass, and clay is used for ceramic.

What are the historic walls of Intramuros made of?

They are built from coral stone and adobe! These are solid, naturally occurring mineral materials.

What are rocks made of?

They are made of one or more minerals that are packed tightly together!

Does matter get lost in the rock cycle?

Nope! Matter is never lost. The exact same materials are just reused over and over again to build brand new rocks!
We use rocks and minerals every day! We build houses and roads, make cement and glass, and get metals like iron and copper.
Fossil fuels hide deep underground or under the sea — coal is dug from mines, while oil and gas are pumped up through drilled wells.
Inside geodes, amethyst often grows side by side with clear quartz or calcite! They grow together because they come from the exact same mineral-rich water.
Minerals and rocks are everywhere! Table salt is halite, jewellery has gold, floors use marble rock, cement comes from limestone, and chalk is gypsum or calcite.

Where do we get materials like gold and gravel?

From mining and quarrying! They dig minerals, rock, and metals out of the ground, like gold, copper, and gravel used in building and industry.
Your thyroid gland needs the mineral iodine to work right, which is found in some rocks and dissolved in seawater!
Filipinos extract natural alum, or tawas, from volcanic minerals! We use this crystalline mineral's astringent properties as a traditional deodorant.
A mineral is a naturally formed, inorganic solid with a specific crystal structure and definite chemical composition. That's why plastic and glass are NOT minerals!

briefs.competency: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
existing_facts_en:
What is a pyroclastic flow?

It's a super-hot, super-fast cloud of gas, ash, and rocks racing down a volcano's slope. It's one of the deadliest volcanic hazards — no one can outrun it!
A pyroclastic flow is a super hot, super fast rush of ash and gas racing down a volcano — and it's extremely deadly!

What is a lahar?

A lahar is volcanic mud and ash mixed with rainwater — it destroyed many towns after Mount Pinatubo erupted!

Why wear a mask when a volcano erupts?

A volcano can throw out a thick cloud of ash that falls as ashfall. Wearing a mask keeps you from breathing it in!

Does a hot spring mean a volcano is about to erupt?

Nope, that’s a misconception! They quietly heat water for thousands of years. The heat just means there’s hot rock below, not an eruption warning!

How do you stay safe near an active volcano?

Stay out of the danger zone! When the alert level is high, evacuate right away. Always wear a mask to protect yourself from ash.

How does ash affect plants and animals?

Ash blocks sunlight from leaves and hurts animals' teeth when they eat coated grass. That's why farmers move animals to safety and cover crops!
Ashfall is slow ash from the sky that you can escape. A pyroclastic flow is a super-hot, super-fast cloud of gas and ash you cannot outrun!
PHIVOLCS sets a Permanent Danger Zone (PDZ) around active volcanoes. For Mayon, the PDZ is 6 km from the crater — no one may live there!

Volcanic ash is harmful to health! Fine ash particles can enter lungs and cause respiratory problems. People in ash-fall areas should wear masks, stay indoors, and clear ash from roofs — wet ash is very heavy and can collapse a house!
After a big volcanic eruption, PHIVOLCS makes lahar hazard zone maps! These show which rivers and valleys might get mudflows, so people can evacuate during heavy rains.
When a volcano like Taal erupts, wear an N95 mask and goggles to prevent fine volcanic ash from irritating your lungs and eyes!
Wearing an N95 mask during volcanic ashfall prevents fine silica particles from entering your lungs and causing breathing problems!
Volcanic ash from Mayon Volcano has tiny rock particles that can damage lungs, so wear an N95 mask to protect your health during an eruption!
Volcanic ash has sharp glass particles that can scratch your corneas, so always wear goggles to protect your eyes during an ashfall!

briefs.competency: make suggestions about the importance of the Sun to living things for a group or class discussion and confirm and record ideas by referring to trustworthy secondary sources
existing_facts_en:
What does sunlight make in your skin?

Sunlight hitting your skin makes vitamin D, which helps build strong bones — your skin works like a tiny factory!
Thanks to the warm Philippine climate, calamansi trees can bear fruit almost all year round.

Which vitamin comes from sunlight?

Vitamin D! Your skin makes it when sunlight hits it.
Sunlight helps your skin make vitamin D from a type of cholesterol, and that vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium for strong bones.

Which vitamin comes from sunlight?

Vitamin D is unusual — it doesn't only come from food. Your own skin makes it when sunlight hits you, so a little morning sun really helps.
Sunlight on your skin makes vitamin D, which helps your bones grow strong -- one more reason morning outdoor play is good for you.
Morning sunlight helps our bodies make vitamin D! This special vitamin gives us super strong and healthy bones.

Why do we need the Sun?

The Sun is our nearest star! It gives the heat and light that plants, animals, and people all need to live on Earth.

Why can plants and animals live on Earth?

Thanks to the Sun! Its light and heat make life on Earth possible, especially for plants and animals.

How does the sun help keep our bones strong?

Sunlight helps our bodies make vitamin D! A little morning sun is great, but be careful in the strong midday sun so your skin doesn't get burned.
The Sun is super hot, but Earth is the perfect distance away so we don't burn! Too close is too hot, too far is too cold. This just-right spot lets life thrive!
The Sun is a star and gives energy to almost all life on Earth! Plants use its light to make food through photosynthesis, and animals eat plants. So, your food actually comes from a star's energy!
Because the Sun is so big and hot, its light and heat reach the whole Earth! This power gives life to plants, animals, and people. If it were small, there wouldn't be enough warmth.
Because the Sun is so powerful, almost all Earth's energy comes from it — the food we eat, the wind, even fuel! Solar panels even take electricity directly from its light.
Expose your arms to direct sunlight for 15 minutes! This helps your body produce Vitamin D to strengthen your bones.

How does native tinawon rice grow in the cool Cordillera terraces?

It relies on intense solar radiation from the sun to drive photosynthesis and grow in the cool highland terraces!

What makes sinigang sour, and when does it fruit?

Sinigang uses tamarind, a crop that fruits abundantly during the dry season when sunlight is most intense!
Human skin requires ultraviolet sunlight to synthesize vitamin D, which helps the body absorb calcium!
The rare waling-waling orchid in Davao needs intense sunlight from our solar system's star to trigger its beautiful blooming cycle!

briefs.competency: predict and explain whether heavier objects will fall faster than lighter objects due to the force of gravity
existing_facts_en:
Do heavy and light objects really fall at the exact same speed when there is no air resistance?

Yes! In free fall, all objects speed up downward at the same acceleration due to gravity, about 9.8 meters per second each second.
Without air resistance, heavy and light objects fall at the exact same rate because gravity gives every mass the same acceleration!
Without air slowing them down, heavy and light objects fall and hit the ground together because gravity speeds them up by the same amount!

Why does paper fall slower than a rock?

A sheet of paper falls slower than a rock because air pushes against the paper, not because gravity is weaker on it!

Do heavy and light things fall at the same speed?

Without air slowing them down, they fall at the exact same speed!
Galileo showed that heavy and light objects fall at the same speed when no air slows them down!
A heavy rock and a light ball fall at the same speed! Without air slowing them down, gravity pulls them equally, so they hit the ground together.
Heavier objects don't fall faster! Without air, a rock and a ball hit the ground together because gravity gives them the same falling speed. Air just makes light things like paper fall slower.
Think heavier objects fall faster? Nope! Without air, a big rock and small rock fall at the same time. A rock beats a feather because of air resistance, not weight!

Does a heavier bob make a pendulum swing faster?

No! If the string length is the same, the swing rate is exactly the same, no matter the bob's weight!

Do heavy and light objects fall at the same speed without air?

Yes! Without air resistance, all objects fall at the same acceleration of 9.8 m/s². In a vacuum, a feather and a hammer fall together!

Do heavy things fall faster than light things?

Nope! Without air resistance, all objects falling toward Earth accelerate at the same rate — about 9.8 m/s² — no matter their mass!
In a vacuum with no air resistance, heavy and light objects fall at the exact same rate, just like Galileo showed!

Why does a feather fall slower than a stone?

Air resistance pushes harder on the feather's light, wide shape! But without air, like on the moon, gravity pulls them both down at the same time.

Why does a feather fall slower than a rock in the air?

Because air resistance pushes back harder on the lightweight feather, making it fall slower!

Will a heavy bowling ball or a light feather fall faster in a vacuum chamber?

They hit the ground at exactly the same time! Gravity accelerates both objects equally inside the vacuum chamber.

Why do heavy, spiky durians fall straight down in Davao orchards?

Earth's gravity pulls falling ripe durian fruits straight down to the ground, regardless of their heavy, spiky mass!
Without air resistance, a bowling ball and a feather dropped from the same height hit the ground at exactly the same time!

Do heavier coconuts fall faster than lighter ones?

Nope! Gravity pulls all falling coconuts toward Earth at the exact same acceleration rate, no matter how heavy or light they are!

briefs.competency: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
existing_facts_en: PAGASA is the Philippine agency that gives warnings about storms and lightning so we can always be prepared!

What should you do when PAGASA warns about a thunderstorm?

When PAGASA issues a severe thunderstorm warning, stay inside your house! Keep away from windows and doors to stay safe from lightning and strong winds.
Weather satellites watch typhoons from space, so PAGASA can warn Filipinos before a storm arrives!

Who watches out for the habagat, amihan, and storms?

PAGASA! It is the government agency that monitors the weather to warn us about heavy rain or storms.
PAGASA uses weather satellites in space to take pictures of clouds and storms from above, helping them see exactly where a storm is heading!

How does PAGASA warn us about typhoon winds?

They raise a Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal from No.1 to No.5! The higher the number, the stronger the wind and greater the danger.

Who warns us about thunderstorms in the Philippines?

PAGASA issues thunderstorm advisories in the Philippines so people can prepare ahead of time!

Why does PAGASA issue storm surge warnings?

To alert coastal communities and keep them safe before a typhoon arrives!
PAGASA's storm surge warnings come in different levels depending on the expected water height, from low to most dangerous!

Who watches the weather in the Philippines?

PAGASA is the government agency that watches the weather and gives warnings about typhoons in the Philippines!

How does PAGASA use rain gauges to keep us safe?

PAGASA tracks how heavy and how much rain falls. When the amount gets very high, they issue a flood warning!

Who watches out for us when a typhoon is on its way?

PAGASA is the agency that warns the whole country! They use wind signals to tell everyone just how strong the wind will be.

When a typhoon comes, PAGASA raises storm signals from No. 1 to No. 5. Higher numbers mean stronger winds and more danger—use them to prepare or know if classes are cancelled. It's a warning to keep everyone safe!
In the Philippines, PAGASA runs weather stations all over the country! From their data, they give the forecasts and typhoon warnings we see on the news!
A weather station sits on the ground, measuring weather at one exact spot. A weather satellite floats in space, photographing clouds and storms from above. Together, they make better forecasts!

How does PAGASA track the eyewall to keep us safe?

PAGASA uses radar and satellites to spot the eyewall and track its path! This helps them warn everyone to prepare and evacuate before danger hits.
A tropical storm is the stage between a tropical depression and a typhoon! Its winds reach 62–88 km/h, and PAGASA gives it a local name.

How do geostationary satellites like Himawari help us watch the weather?

Geostationary satellites like Japan's Himawari stay above a fixed point on Earth. They send continuous images of clouds and typhoons over the Philippines and Asia every ten minutes!

Why does PAGASA issue storm warning signals?

They issue these signals before and during a typhoon so we know how strong the winds will be and when to take cover!

How can your family stay safe before a typhoon?

Prepare clean water, long-lasting food, a flashlight, and medicine! Always follow PAGASA warnings to keep everyone safe.

What should families do when PAGASA raises Public Storm Warning Signal Number 1?

Secure loose roofs! Winds of 39 to 61 kph are expected during this warning signal.
A barometer measures atmospheric pressure to help meteorologists predict if a low-pressure area will bring rain!

briefs.competency: explain how natural objects in the sky affect activities of people
existing_facts_en:
How did people tell time before clocks existed?

A shadow moves as the sun crosses the sky! Long ago, people used a sundial to track that shadow and tell time.
A sundial uses the moving shadow cast by the sun to tell the time!
A sundial is a super cool ancient clock that tells time just by using the shadow cast by the sun!
Strong outbursts from the Sun can disturb Earth's magnetic field! This can affect electricity, GPS, and satellite signals.
The Moon's pull causes ocean tides to rise and fall, and they are strongest at new and full moons!
Many Filipino fishermen watch the tides caused by the Moon. They know when the water is highest or lowest to catch more fish!

How did people know the season before calendars existed?

They watched the stars! Orion appears during cool months, so seeing it meant the cool season arrived. Different constellations show up depending on where Earth is in its orbit.

Why do Filipino fishermen watch the tide table?

At low tide, shells and small fish are exposed along the shore, making them easy to gather! The PAGASA tide table helps them know when.

Why do ships watch the tide times?

At high tide, harbor water gets deeper! This helps big ships enter and leave easily without scraping the bottom.
On a sundial, the rod's shadow points to the time. But because of the penumbra, the shadow's tip is blurry, making the exact time a bit hard to read!

How did people tell time before clocks?

A sundial is one of the earliest clocks! It tells time by where the shadow of an upright part falls on a marked plate.
Stay away from the shoreline during a spring tide, as the aligned Sun and Moon create unusually high, dangerous waves!

Why are full moon beaches dangerous for swimmers?

During a full moon, higher high tides called spring tides can unexpectedly sweep swimmers away!
Knowing that a full moon causes higher tides helps beachgoers avoid getting trapped by sudden rising water!

How do local fishermen in Manila Bay use the moon?

The moon's gravitational pull creates high tides that they use to navigate their wooden fishing boats!
Traditional Filipino fisherfolk track the moon's phases because the lunar gravitational pull creates the ocean tides they navigate to catch fish!

Why do Filipinos traditionally take a siesta at noon?

It aligns with Earth's rotation! The sun reaches its highest, hottest point at noon, making it the perfect time to rest.
Ancient Filipino sailors used constellations like the North Star to navigate their wooden balangay boats across the vast ocean!
During a full moon, stronger spring tides happen in towns like Lingayen, bringing nutrient-rich deep waters closer to shore for fishermen!

What causes the highest high tides during the lunar cycle?

During the spring tide phase, the Sun, Earth, and Moon align to produce the highest high tides!

Why do we feel sleepy at night?

When Earth's rotation brings darkness, our brain releases a hormone called melatonin to make us feel sleepy!
Solar flares can disrupt satellite signals! That's why keeping a battery-powered radio ensures you still receive emergency typhoon warnings.
Fishermen in the Philippines plan their night fishing trips around the full moon because its gravity creates the highest tides!

Why does Earth's rotation affect how we sleep?

Earth's 24-hour rotation creates the day-night cycle that regulates melatonin production in the brain—a hormone controlling our sleep and wake patterns!
Because Earth rotates eastward, eastern cities like Davao see the sunrise earlier each day than western cities like Manila!

briefs.competency: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
existing_facts_en: During floods or typhoons, stay away from deep, fast-moving water — it can easily cause drowning, so follow PAGASA warnings and evacuate if needed!
During typhoons in the Philippines, brownouts happen! Candles make great emergency lights because they need no battery or socket. Always keep candles and matches ready at home before a strong storm!
Before a typhoon arrives, barometric pressure drops! This warns us of severe storms. PAGASA uses barometers across the Philippines to detect these pressure changes and forecast the weather.

What happens to the habagat when a typhoon is near?

It gets even stronger! This makes the rain over the Philippines much, much heavier.

How does PAGASA warn us about typhoon winds?

They raise a Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal from No.1 to No.5! The higher the number, the stronger the wind and greater the danger.

What is a storm surge?

A storm surge is when a typhoon pushes the ocean, making seawater rise up and flood coastal areas!
Rainbands are spiraling lines of thick rain clouds. They wrap all the way around the eye of the typhoon!
A storm surge is a sudden rise of seawater! Strong typhoon winds push it onto the coast, causing serious flooding.

How do the eyewall's strong winds affect the ocean?

The eyewall's super strong winds push ocean water toward the shore, making the sea suddenly rise! This dangerous rise is called a storm surge, threatening coastal towns.
Inside the eyewall, air pressure is the lowest in the whole storm! This huge pressure difference sucks air inward super fast, creating the eyewall's incredibly powerful winds.

What does a typhoon look like from space?

A satellite shows spiral cloud bands centered on the eye, carrying heavy rain and strong winds!
The typhoon eye is a surprisingly calm spot in the storm's center! It has clear skies and low pressure because sinking air stops clouds from forming.

How does a tropical cyclone grow and end?

It goes through stages: tropical disturbance, tropical depression, tropical storm, and typhoon! It can disappear at any stage if it hits land or ocean conditions change.

What is rapid intensification in a typhoon?

It happens when a typhoon suddenly strengthens by 55 km/h or more in 24 hours, making forecasting harder and giving people less time to prepare!

What does a typhoon's 'eye' tell us in a satellite image?

Thick white clouds show intense conditions, and the small clear hole at the center—the eye—reveals how organized and strong the storm is.

Why does PAGASA issue storm warning signals?

They issue these signals before and during a typhoon so we know how strong the winds will be and when to take cover!

What is inside a strong typhoon?

At its center is a quiet, calm region called the eye! Surrounding it is the eyewall, which holds the strongest winds and rain.
Seen from a satellite in space, a typhoon looks like a giant swirling spiral of clouds spinning around the calm eye at its center!
A typhoon has three main parts: the calm eye at the center, the eyewall with the strongest winds, and the spiral rainbands carrying rain around the outside!

What pushes a massive wall of ocean water onto land during a strong typhoon?

A storm surge! It pushes that huge wall of water right onto the land.

What happens during a storm surge?

It pushes seawater inland during a typhoon! If there's a surge warning, evacuate to higher ground immediately.
Pack a go-bag with a battery-powered radio, flashlight, and first-aid kit to keep your family informed and safe when a typhoon cuts off electricity!
In the mature stage of a cumulonimbus cloud, heavy rain and hail fall while strong updrafts and downdrafts happen at the same time inside the storm!

What does a sudden drop in air pressure mean?

It signals an approaching typhoon! You should secure loose roofs and bring your pets indoors safely.
Always store drinking water before a typhoon arrives! Strong winds and floods can easily destroy local water pipes and contaminate the water pumps.

briefs.competency: explain how light and sound can be harmful to people and make suggestions on how to protect oneself from them
existing_facts_en: Very loud sounds can damage the tiny parts inside your ear and weaken your hearing.
A hat, long sleeves, or an umbrella all help protect your skin from the sun's rays!

Why do city lights hurt fireflies?

Too much bright light in cities makes it hard for fireflies to see each other's blinking signals.
Sunscreen protects skin from the sun's harmful rays, which can cause burns and damage.
Sunscreen protects your skin by absorbing or reflecting harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun before it damages cells!
Super loud sounds can actually hurt your ears! That's why it's smart to stay away from noises that are too intense.

Where is the safest place during a lightning storm?

Go inside a building and avoid standing under a tree!
Safety first! Never look at the sun through a convex lens. It concentrates rays into a super hot point that can burn paper and seriously damage your eyes!

What's the '30-30 rule' for lightning safety?

Count the seconds between flash and thunder! If it's under 30 seconds, go inside NOW! Then wait 30 minutes after the last thunder before going out.
You can touch an LED bulb even after hours! Almost all electricity turns into light, not heat. Old bulbs, however, get way too hot to touch safely!
Sound intensity is measured in decibels (dB)! Normal conversation is about 60 dB, a noisy road is 80 dB, and sounds above 85 dB can damage hearing.
In our hot climate, hats and umbrellas protect your skin from the Sun's ultraviolet radiation! This reduces sunburn and heat-related illness.

Why do baby pawikan get lost at night?

Baby pawikan hatchlings follow the brightest night sky to the sea! But artificial light from resorts and roads disorients them, leading them away from the ocean.

How do earplugs protect your hearing near loud machines?

They block high-energy sound waves! This protects the delicate hair cells in your inner ear from permanent hearing loss.
Listening to loud music through earphones for a long time can permanently damage the tiny hair cells inside your ears!
Wearing earplugs near loud karaoke machines reduces sound energy intensity, protecting your eardrums from permanent hearing damage.
Listening to loud headphone audio for over an hour daily can permanently damage the delicate hair cells in your ears!

What is the safest light to use during a brownout?

A battery-powered flashlight! It prevents the fire hazards of lighting open-flame candles during a power outage.

Why shouldn't you stare at a solar eclipse?

The intense light can permanently burn your retinas if you look without certified eclipse glasses!
Never look directly at the sun! Its intense visible light and ultraviolet rays can burn eye tissue and damage your retina.

Why does reading in dim light give you a headache?

Reading in dim light forces your eye muscles to work harder, causing temporary eye strain and headaches!

Is ozone always good for us?

Ozone is good high up to filter UV, but bad near the ground where it becomes part of air pollution!
Even though mountain air is cold, your skin can sunburn more easily there — thin air lets more of the Sun's strong rays reach you!
High up in the sky, the ozone layer acts like a shield! It is a thin layer of gas that blocks the Sun's harmful ultraviolet rays.

Why do we need sunscreen on sunny days?

Earth's ozone layer blocks the Sun's ultraviolet radiation, so applying sunscreen protects your skin from harmful sunburns!

Want to observe the solar system safely?

Never look directly at the sun without certified eclipse glasses! This prevents permanent eye damage while you explore.

Why is it dangerous to look at a solar eclipse without special glasses?

Looking directly at a solar eclipse without special glasses can permanently damage your retinas and cause blindness!
Unlike the sun, looking directly at the bright full moon will not permanently damage your eyes!
Never stare directly at the Sun during a solar eclipse! It can permanently damage your retina, the light-sensitive tissue at the back of your eye.

briefs.competency: describe safety measures that people can use to avoid the harmful effects of the Sun's light
existing_facts_en: A hat, long sleeves, or an umbrella all help protect your skin from the sun's rays!
Pale or pink pigs can get sunburned easily, so they wallow in mud to protect their skin.
Sunscreen protects skin from the sun's harmful rays, which can cause burns and damage.
The salakot is a traditional Filipino hat with a wide brim that shades the face and neck from the burning sun.
Sunscreen protects your skin by absorbing or reflecting harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun before it damages cells!
In our hot climate, hats and umbrellas protect your skin from the Sun's ultraviolet radiation! This reduces sunburn and heat-related illness.

Why shouldn't you stare at a solar eclipse?

The intense light can permanently burn your retinas if you look without certified eclipse glasses!
Never look directly at the sun! Its intense visible light and ultraviolet rays can burn eye tissue and damage your retina.
Never look directly at the Sun during a solar eclipse! Its bright light is very strong and can easily damage your eyes.
A lunar eclipse is totally safe to watch with your bare eyes! The Moon's light is very gentle and soft, unlike the Sun's.
Never look straight at the Sun during a solar eclipse, because those bright rays can damage your eyes!

How can you safely watch a solar eclipse?

Use special eclipse glasses or a pinhole projector! Ordinary sunglasses are NOT safe enough.

How does the ozone layer protect us from UV rays?

Ozone soaks up UV energy! When UV hits it, the ozone molecule briefly breaks apart and turns the energy into heat. Then it re-forms, ready to do it all again.

Is all ozone bad for us?

High-up ozone in the stratosphere is good—it shields us from UV! But ground-level ozone is bad; it harms our lungs and is part of city smog.
If the ozone layer suddenly disappeared, way too much UV would reach the ground! It would cause more sunburn, skin and eye problems, and damage plants and tiny sea animals too.
The ozone layer is super important, but it's actually very thin! If you squished all the ozone together, it would be thinner than two stacked coins.

How does the sun help keep our bones strong?

Sunlight helps our bodies make vitamin D! A little morning sun is great, but be careful in the strong midday sun so your skin doesn't get burned.

Can you look at the Sun during a solar eclipse?

Never look straight at it! It can damage your eyes. Use special eclipse glasses, or just watch its shadow projected on paper.

Which layer protects Earth from harmful UV radiation?

The stratosphere! It is the second layer of the atmosphere (12–50 km) and contains the ozone layer.

Why is the UV index so high in the Philippines?

It's close to the equator with a high sun angle! Always wear sunscreen and a hat outdoors for sun protection.

How can you watch an eclipse safely without looking straight at the sun?

Use a pinhole projector! Sunlight passes through a tiny hole to cast a small image of the sun on paper.

Is it safe to look at a solar eclipse with bare eyes?

Never! Even if the sun is mostly covered, the tiny part still showing can burn your eyes.

How can you protect your skin from painful sunburns during outdoor recess?

Apply broad-spectrum sunscreen before going out! It blocks the sun's harmful ultraviolet rays that cause painful sunburns.
Drinking plenty of water and resting in the shade prevents heatstroke when extreme summer temperatures cause dangerous heatwaves!

Why do we need sunscreen on sunny days?

Earth's ozone layer blocks the Sun's ultraviolet radiation, so applying sunscreen protects your skin from harmful sunburns!

Want to observe the solar system safely?

Never look directly at the sun without certified eclipse glasses! This prevents permanent eye damage while you explore.

Why is it dangerous to look at a solar eclipse without special glasses?

Looking directly at a solar eclipse without special glasses can permanently damage your retinas and cause blindness!
Drink plenty of water and stay in the shade when the heat index exceeds 40°C to prevent heatstroke!

How can you prevent heatstroke during the dry season?

Drink plenty of water! This prevents heatstroke, which happens when your body overheats from extreme sun exposure.
Earth's atmosphere blocks most harmful solar radiation, but you still need sunscreen to protect your skin from the Sun's ultraviolet rays!
The ozone layer shields us from the sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) rays. Without it, sunlight would be very dangerous to our skin and eyes!
Moderate exposure to sunlight helps your skin synthesize vitamin D, which your body absorbs to maintain healthy teeth!
Never stare directly at the Sun during a solar eclipse! It can permanently damage your retina, the light-sensitive tissue at the back of your eye.

briefs.competency: explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons
existing_facts_en: Orion is a famous constellation shaped like a hunter, with three stars in a row called Orion's Belt. In the Philippines, some native stories call it Balatik — a hunting trap!

What is the Big Dipper and how can it help you find other stars?

The Big Dipper is seven bright stars shaped like a big ladle! Part of Ursa Major (the Great Bear), it's super easy to use as a guide to find other stars.
The Southern Cross (Crux) is a small, cross-shaped constellation in the southern sky! People use it to find the direction of south.

How did Filipino farmers know when to plant crops?

Long ago, they used constellations like Balatik as a sky calendar! Their appearance signaled the coming of the rains.
A constellation is a star pattern that draws a picture in the sky! These same star pictures slowly move across the night sky every evening.
The stars in a constellation only look close together, but they are really very far apart in space.

When can we see Orion in the Philippines?

In the Philippines, Orion can often be seen at night during the months of December to February!
Use the two end stars of the Big Dipper as pointers to find Polaris, the North Star!
A constellation is a cool pattern or shape formed by a group of stars in the night sky!

Did early Filipinos have their own star patterns?

Yes! Long before telescopes, early Filipinos named star groupings like Balatik after a hunting trap. Farmers and fishermen used these patterns to guide their seasons!
Orion is named after a Greek hunter! Connect its stars to see a person with a belt, raised arm, and club or bow. It's just a picture imagined in the sky!
Orion looks like a hunter with a belt, while the Big Dipper looks like a big ladle with a handle. Each constellation has its own unique story and shape!

How did people know the season before calendars existed?

They watched the stars! Orion appears during cool months, so seeing it meant the cool season arrived. Different constellations show up depending on where Earth is in its orbit.
A constellation is a group of stars forming shapes like animals or people! Long ago, they helped tell stories and find direction. But these stars aren't close; they just line up from Earth!
The Southern Cross (Crux) is a famous constellation in the southern hemisphere! In the Philippines, you can spot it during winter months. Pacific Island navigators used it to find south!
A constellation is a group of stars forming a picture pattern in the sky, named by ancient people like Orion and the Southern Cross. They used it to guide travel and farming!
The Big Dipper is seven bright stars shaped like a ladle, and its two end stars point to the North Star to show which way is north!
Did you know the Big Dipper is actually just a part of the huge Ursa Major constellation, which means the Great Bear!
You can easily find Polaris, the North Star, just by using the two outer stars of the Big Dipper!

What kind of star is Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion?

Betelgeuse is a huge red supergiant star located in the constellation Orion!

What is the official name of the Southern Cross constellation?

The Southern Cross is actually a constellation officially called Crux!

Want to find your way south?

Just look for the Southern Cross! It is used to find the direction south.

Who is the famous hunter in the sky?

It's the constellation Orion! It is called 'the Hunter' or ang Mangangaso.
Look at the Southern Cross (Crux)! It has four (4) main stars forming a perfect cross shape.

How do people find south in the night sky?

By looking for the Southern Cross (Crux)! It's a small cross-shaped constellation in the southern sky that points to the direction of south.
The three bright stars of the Balatik constellation are actually massive, hot blue supergiants! They are part of Orion and live far beyond our solar system.
Stars in a constellation look close together from Earth! But in space, they can actually be hundreds of light-years apart from each other.

How do the Tagbanua people of Palawan use the stars?

They use the Balatik constellation, the local name for Orion’s Belt, to navigate and track the seasons!
Ancient Filipino sailors used constellations like the North Star to navigate their wooden balangay boats across the vast ocean!
The Tagbanua people of Palawan recognize the Balatik constellation, which is the same as the Orion constellation in Western astronomy!
The ancient Tagalogs named the Orion constellation Balatik, using it to track the changing seasons in the Philippines!
Stars looking close in a constellation, like the Big Dipper, can actually be many light-years apart in space!
Filipinos call the Orion constellation "Balatik"! It is a prominent three-star pattern that is super visible during the dry season.

briefs.competency: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
existing_facts_en: Oxygen is the gas that helps things burn! When a flame uses up all the oxygen around it, poof — the flame goes out!
Carbon dioxide is the fizzy gas in soft drinks and the gas we breathe out! You can test for it because it turns limewater cloudy.
Cover a lit candle with a jar, and the flame dies once the oxygen inside is used up!

What three things do you need to make a fire?

To make a fire, you need three things: fuel, heat, and oxygen!
The gas that pops out when baking soda meets vinegar is called carbon dioxide!

Why can this gas put out a small candle flame?

The carbon dioxide from the reaction is heavier than air, so it sinks and snuffs out small candle flames!

Is the gas we breathe out the same as this one?

The carbon dioxide made by baking soda and vinegar is the exact same gas we breathe out!

What is the difference between air and a vacuum?

Air is full of gas particles, but a vacuum has no air at all! Outer space is nearly a vacuum, so there is no sound there.

What is inside a balloon when you blow it up?

It fills with your exhaled breath! This is a mix of nitrogen, oxygen, and more carbon dioxide, because your body already used up some oxygen.
Not all of the greenhouse effect is bad! Without some carbon dioxide in the air, Earth would freeze over. The natural greenhouse effect keeps our temperature comfortable enough for life to thrive.
We breathe in Oxygen to live, not carbon dioxide! We breathe out CO2. A little CO2 isn't poison, but too much in the atmosphere warms our world.
The air we breathe is a homogeneous mixture of gases like nitrogen and oxygen! You can't see or separate them because they mix evenly. Anywhere in a room, the air is exactly the same!
Smog is a dirty haze of smoke and gases from vehicles and factories. It harms our lungs and makes breathing much harder!
A helium balloon floats because helium is less dense than the surrounding air! Buoyancy works in the air, not just in water.
Water vapor is in the air even though we can't see it! It's a completely transparent gas, and humidity is simply the measure of how much water vapor is in the air.

How do CO2 fire extinguishers put out fires?

They release CO2 to smother flames by displacing oxygen! It's super safe for electrical fires because CO2 doesn't conduct electricity.
Ozone (O3) is a special oxygen in the stratosphere, 15-35 kilometers above Earth! It acts like a shield, protecting us from the sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

How can you put out a fire by removing oxygen?

You can cover a small fire with a fire blanket, or use a CO2 extinguisher to replace the oxygen around the flames with CO2!
PM2.5 are tiny air particles less than 2.5 micrometres wide! They are too small to see, but they can sneak deep into our lungs and cause health problems.

Why is breathing too much helium from a balloon dangerous?

Breathing helium displaces oxygen in your lungs! Inhaling too much of this lighter gas can cause dangerous fainting.

What gases come out of a traditional jeepney engine's exhaust?

The exhaust from a traditional jeepney engine is a mixture of gases like carbon dioxide and water vapor!
Air is a homogeneous mixture of gases, meaning it is a gaseous solution containing nitrogen and oxygen!
HEPA air filters trap solid dust particles and pollen from the indoor air gas mixture!

How do N95 masks protect our lungs?

N95 masks filter out solid dust particles from the air, keeping our lungs safe from pollution!

What's hiding inside the limestone caves of the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River?

It holds trapped air, a gaseous mixture of oxygen and nitrogen, inside its limestone caves!

How does the Philippine eagle fly?

It relies on the physical properties of air, a mixture of gases, to generate lift for its wings!
After breathing, a Philippine eagle exhales water vapor, which is simply water in a gaseous state!

What do our lungs exchange when we breathe?

They exchange gaseous oxygen from inhaled air with gaseous carbon dioxide from cellular respiration!
During cellular respiration, the Philippine tarsier exhales carbon dioxide gas right into the air!
Your lungs are gas exchangers! They take in oxygen gas from the air and release carbon dioxide gas back into the environment.
Your lungs exchange gases! They absorb oxygen from inhaled air and release carbon dioxide when you exhale.

What wraps around Earth like a giant invisible blanket?

The atmosphere! It's a thick layer of air holding our oxygen, keeping temperatures just right, and shielding us from the Sun's harmful rays. It has different layers.
The Perseverance rover was the first to make oxygen on Mars! It pulled oxygen from the carbon dioxide in the air, which could one day help astronauts breathe.

Why do hot springs have bubbles?

Gases like carbon dioxide escape from rocks below! The gas rises and bubbles up because it is lighter than water, not just from boiling.

What's inside fossil fuels that makes them burn?

They're packed with carbon and hydrogen from ancient life — these release heat when burned, but the carbon also escapes as carbon dioxide into the air.

How thick is the ozone layer?

Even though it's super important, the ozone layer is actually thin compared to the whole atmosphere! There's only a little ozone in the air, but it's enough to block lots of UV.
When rain falls, it mixes with carbon dioxide from the air and soil, becoming slightly acidic. This weakly acidic water is what slowly dissolves limestone over time!
Limestone caves can trap heavy carbon dioxide gas near the floor, which might suffocate you if you crawl inside!
